# The data catalog vocabulary

> DCAT is an RDF vocabulary designed to facilitate interoperability between data catalogs published on the Web. By using DCAT to describe datasets in data catalogs, publishers increase discoverability and enable applications easily to consume metadata from multiple catalogs. It further enables decentralized publishing of catalogs and facilitates federated dataset search across sites. Aggregated DCAT metadata can serve as a manifest file to facilitate digital preservation. DCAT is defined at http://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-dcat/. Any variance between that normative document and this schema is an error

- Ontology IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat
- Namespace: http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat# (prefix `dcat:`)
- Version: 3
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Contents: 9 classes, 30 object properties, 9 datatype properties, 27 annotation properties

Terms are identified by IRI; use the CURIEs and labels below when writing SPARQL or RDF.

## Documentation

- [Overview](index.md): metadata and contents
- [Classes](classes.md): 9 classes with definitions and axioms
- [Object properties](object-properties.md): 30 object properties with definitions and axioms
- [Datatype properties](datatype-properties.md): 9 datatype properties with definitions and axioms
- [Annotation properties](annotation-properties.md): 27 annotation properties with definitions and axioms

## Machine-readable

- [ontology.json](ontology.json): all terms as JSON (IRI, label, definition, hierarchy, domain/range)
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): the complete documentation as one Markdown file
- [Turtle](ontology.ttl): the ontology source (text/turtle)
- [RDF/XML](ontology.owl): the ontology source (application/rdf+xml)
- [JSON-LD](ontology.jsonld): the ontology source (application/ld+json)
- [N-Triples](ontology.nt): the ontology source (application/n-triples)
